main_text.p: bi de seipso, Ego, inquit, sum ex filiis filiorum ipsius Ra-chel. Quicquid horum verius, inquit Iudæus ille, cum venerit, ipse indicabit nobis.

Translatus] Iudæorum vulgus & sapientes credunt eum translatum in hortum Eden, hoc est in Paradisum, ibique vivere cum anima & corpore: a quibus diversi abeunt recentiores Rabbini, & in his R. David, qui scribit eum turbine raptum e terra in aerem usque ad sphæram ignis, ibique consumptum corpus ejus, spiritum autem rediisse ad Deum, qui dedit ipsum.

Helisæus] scribo. Elisæum; quod factum putarim ex Hebræo Elisæ Latina declinatione. Nam ex Græco Ἐλισαῖος [?] esset Elisæus, cum diphthongo. Quanquam in editione Romana Ἐλισαῖ [?]. אֱלִישָׁע [?] Elisa, & ἐλισαῖος [?] Elisæ, ut יְלִישָׁע [?] Thare.

Multis signis potens] apud Nicolaum de Lyra recensentur miracula sedecim edita ab Elisæo, cum Elias tantum octo ediderit. Quo accommodant duplum, quo præditus fuit, spiritum Elisæi. Quem tamen locum alij aliter enarrant. Habetur autem, 4.Reg.2.9.
Ab eo est viduæ filius resuscitatus] enumerat nunc aliquot signa sive miracula Elisæi, sed plura Scholastici recensent ex libris Ebræorum.
main_text.head: Sedecim Elisæi miracula.
main_text.l: 13. Oculorum pueri sui apertio ad videndum equos & currus igneos &c.
15. Abundantia commeatus inopinata in porta Samariæ.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek words Ἐλισαῖος, Ἐλισαῖ and ἐλισαῖος, and the Hebrew words אֱלִישָׁע and יְלִישָׁע, are hard to read at this scan resolution and are marked [?]. "Thare" after the Hebrew is printed as it appears but is uncertain. "Gtezi" in item 11 is uncertain (probably Gehazi) and is marked [?]. The first word of the page ("bi") is a fragment from the previous page and may be misread. The line "13." breaks at "cur-" and continues on the next line as "rus". The printed "16. Suf-" is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
